_about: DAOasis Journey V2 — one architecture for every Journey. Journey 1 and Journey 20 are the same shape: add an object to `journeys`, supply stages, and every screen and page renders it. Nothing in the App or website is hard-coded to Everest. Items marked concept:true or approx:true are for review and are NOT approved product decisions.

contribution_model.status: CONCEPT — requires approval. No scoring formula is defined or implied; figures shown in the prototypes are illustrative.

layers.name: Route
layers.question: Where am I?
layers.plain: Movement carries you along the route.

layers.name: Readiness
layers.question: Am I ready for what comes next?
layers.plain: Sleep, breath, water and recovery decide when the next stage opens.

layers.name: Discovery
layers.question: What am I taking from this place?
layers.plain: Learning and reflection unlock the story of each stage.

principles: Rest is part of the Journey. At rest stages the route does not advance; Readiness does.
A comfortable daily distance applies on every Journey. Going past it does not carry you further — the mountain does not reward overreach. (Concept: the cap itself is not set.)
Consistency is a rhythm, not a streak. Missing a day pauses; it never resets or punishes.
Everything here is a digital Journey inspired by a real route. Nobody has travelled there.

journeys.name: Everest Base Camp
journeys.description: The classic Khumbu trek, from the airstrip at Lukla to the foot of the Khumbu Icefall. Seven stages, two days of acclimatisation, and a mountain that rewards patience.
journeys.distance_note: Lukla to Base Camp, one way. The previously published 130 km is the return trek; the descent is modelled as an optional continuation (see open decisions).
journeys.typical_days_real_world: 12–14 days on foot, including two acclimatisation days
journeys.digital_notice: A digital Journey inspired by the real Khumbu route. You are not travelling to Nepal.

stages.name: Lukla
stages.title: The airstrip in the hillside
stages.story: Every Khumbu Journey begins on a short, sloping runway cut into the mountainside. From here there are no roads — only the trail, the river and the people who have used both for centuries.
stages.learning: Starting slowly: why the first day is the one to under-do.
stages.reflection: What are you carrying that you could set down before you begin?

stages.name: Namche Bazaar
stages.title: The amphitheatre town
stages.story: A Sherpa trading town built in a horseshoe of terraced hillside. It is the first place the route asks you to stop — a full day here, higher walks and lower sleeps, while the body begins to adapt.
stages.learning: How the body adapts to altitude — and why slower is faster.
stages.reflection: Where in your life is stopping the stronger move?

stages.name: Tengboche
stages.title: The monastery on the ridge
stages.story: Rhododendron forest gives way to a ridge crowned by the largest monastery in the Khumbu. Ama Dablam stands directly across the valley. Many walkers sit here for a long time.
stages.learning: Slow breathing at height: the nose, the exhale, the pause.
stages.reflection: What would it mean to be quiet for ten minutes here?

stages.name: Dingboche
stages.title: Stone-walled fields, thin air
stages.story: A summer settlement in the Imja valley, its fields divided by low stone walls against the wind. The second acclimatisation day. Sleep gets lighter here; the work is to let it.
stages.learning: Sleep at altitude: what changes, and what helps.
stages.reflection: What has this Journey already taught you about pace?

stages.name: Lobuche
stages.title: The memorial ridge
stages.story: Beside the glacier's moraine, a ridge of stone cairns remembers climbers who did not come home. It is a place for quiet respect on the way up.
stages.learning: Hydration when thirst stops telling the truth.
stages.reflection: Who has helped you reach this far?

stages.name: Gorak Shep
stages.title: The last settlement
stages.story: The final few buildings before the glacier. The old base camp of the early expeditions was once here. Tomorrow's walk is short; the work today is to arrive well.
stages.learning: Recovery: why the last stage is won the night before.
stages.reflection: What does "arriving well" mean to you?

stages.name: Everest Base Camp
stages.title: The foot of the Icefall
stages.story: Prayer flags, tents in season and the broken blue of the Khumbu Icefall above. The summit itself is hidden behind Nuptse. This is not the top of anything — it is the place where the mountain begins.
stages.learning: What changes when you stop climbing and start remembering.
stages.reflection: What will you carry back down?
stages.milestone: Journey complete — the next Journey opens

journeys.label: Flagship Journey · Nepal

journeys.name: Bangkok to Phuket
journeys.description: Walk the length of Thailand, from the capital to the place the Sanctuary is planned. The Journey that started it all — retained exactly as published, now one Journey among many.
journeys.typical_days_real_world: About five months at the app's 8,000-step pace (6 km a day)
journeys.digital_notice: A digital Journey inspired by a real route. You are not travelling to Thailand.
journeys.route_note: Six canonical stages, as published on the website, app and investor materials. The brief for V2 also named Ranong; it is not on the published route and sits on the opposite coast to Surat Thani. See open decisions.

stages.name: Bangkok
stages.title: The capital, before it wakes
stages.story: A city of canals, temples and traffic, seen at the hour before any of it starts. The Journey begins at the river.
stages.reflection: What do you want this Journey to change?

stages.name: Ayutthaya
stages.title: The old capital
stages.story: Brick towers and headless Buddhas in a city that was once among the largest in the world. A reminder that places last longer than plans.
stages.reflection: What has lasted in your life?

stages.name: Hua Hin
stages.title: The royal coast
stages.story: A long beach, a rest stop on the way south, and the first time the Gulf stays beside you for days.
stages.learning: Rest as part of the route.
stages.reflection: When did you last do nothing, well?

stages.name: Surat Thani
stages.title: The gateway to the islands
stages.story: River, mangrove and the ferries out to the islands. The peninsula narrows from here.
stages.reflection: What is the distance between where you started and now?

stages.name: Khao Lak
stages.title: The Andaman coast
stages.story: The route crosses to the other sea. Forest runs down to the shore and the light changes.
stages.reflection: What do you want to remember from the walk?

stages.name: Phuket
stages.title: The island at the end of the road
stages.story: The Journey arrives where the Sanctuary is planned — a real place that is still in development. Arriving here opens the next Journey.
stages.reflection: What comes next?
stages.milestone: Journey complete — the next Journey opens

rewards.note: Milestone recognition in DRC. Amounts are not set.

journeys.label: Journey 01 · Thailand

journeys.role: Example of a Journey in another country
journeys.name: Land's End to John o' Groats
journeys.description: Britain end to end — a test of consistency rather than altitude. Moorland, border country, the Pennines, the Highlands, and no shortcuts.
journeys.distance_note: 1,407 km is the figure already published on the app page. Stage kilometres are indicative, spaced proportionally along the waymarked End to End Trail, and must be set from the final route before production.
journeys.typical_days_real_world: Walkers take two to three months on the full trail
journeys.digital_notice: A digital Journey inspired by a real route. You are not travelling to Britain.

stages.name: Land's End
stages.title: The last of England
stages.story: Granite cliffs, the Atlantic on three sides, and a signpost that points a very long way north.
stages.learning: Setting a pace you can keep.
stages.reflection: What does a long pace look like for you?

stages.name: Barnstaple
stages.title: The coast path ends
stages.story: The south-west coast gives way to Exmoor and the river towns of north Devon.
stages.reflection: What did the first fortnight teach you?

stages.name: Knighton
stages.title: Border country
stages.story: Hills along the line of Offa's Dyke, where England and Wales have been a conversation for a thousand years.
stages.reflection: What do you do when progress is quiet?

stages.name: Hebden Bridge
stages.title: The Pennines
stages.story: Mill towns in steep valleys and the high, wild line of the Pennine Way above them.
stages.reflection: What are you most proud of so far?

stages.name: Jedburgh
stages.title: Into Scotland
stages.story: Abbey ruins and the Scottish Borders. The country opens out.
stages.reflection: What has become easier?

stages.name: Fort William
stages.title: Under Ben Nevis
stages.story: The foot of Britain's highest mountain and the end of the West Highland Way.
stages.reflection: What do you want to finish well?

stages.name: John o' Groats
stages.title: The far north-east corner
stages.story: A harbour, a signpost and nowhere further to go on the mainland. Arriving opens the next Journey.
stages.learning: What a long journey leaves behind.
stages.reflection: What comes next?
stages.milestone: Journey complete — the next Journey opens

journeys.name: DAOasis Foundation
journeys.description: An optional 30-day Journey that teaches how every other Journey works: movement carries you, rest and breath open the way, learning and reflection tell the story. Not mandatory.
journeys.digital_notice: A short, abstract teaching Journey with no real-world location.

stages.name: Week 1 — Begin
stages.title: Begin
stages.story: Move a little each day. Notice how you feel.
stages.reflection: Why are you here?

stages.name: Week 2 — Rest
stages.title: Rest
stages.story: A week where rest counts as much as movement.
stages.reflection: What does rest give you?

stages.name: Week 3 — Breathe
stages.title: Breathe
stages.story: Breath and water open the way forward.
stages.reflection: When do you hold your breath?

stages.name: Week 4 — Arrive
stages.title: Arrive
stages.story: Arrive at the first of many.
stages.reflection: Which Journey calls you?
stages.milestone: Foundation complete — choose your next Journey
